messages.content: Calculate the standard deviation of the null hypothesis test with a sample mean of 98.2, standard deviation of 1.4, and sample size of 40 for a population mean of 98.6.

function.name: statistics_calculate_p_value
function.description: Calculate the p-value for a t-test on a single sample from a population. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

sample_mean.description: The mean of the sample data. This is a float type value.

population_mean.description: The mean of the population data. This is a float type value.

sample_std_dev.description: The standard deviation of the sample data. This is a float type value.

sample_size.description: The size of the sample data.

two_tailed.description: Whether the test is two-tailed. If not provided, default is true.

message.reasoning:
The user asks: "Calculate the standard deviation of the null hypothesis test with a sample mean of 98.2, standard deviation of 1.4, and sample size of 40 for a population mean of 98.6."

They want the standard deviation of the null hypothesis test. That likely refers to the standard error of the mean under the null hypothesis? Usually, the standard error of the sample mean is sample_std_dev / sqrt(sample_size). But if we are doing a t-test, we might use the sample standard deviation as estimate of population standard deviation. The standard error of the mean is s / sqrt(n). So s=1.4, n=40, so SE = 1.4 / sqrt(40) = 1.4 / 6.3249 = about 0.2214. That is the standard error. But the question says "standard deviation of the null hypothesis test". Might be the standard deviation of the sampling distribution of the sample mean under the null hypothesis. That is indeed the standard error. So answer: approximately 0.221.

Alternatively, maybe they want the standard deviation of the t-statistic? That would be sqrt((n-1)/n) * s? No, that's not typical. The t-statistic has standard deviation sqrt(n/(n-1))? Actually, t-statistic distribution has variance n/(n-2) for df=n-1. But that's not what they ask.

Thus answer: 0.221. Provide explanation.
